items.q: The interviewee lists names but does not speak about Buddy Bolden. The mention of Buddy Bolden occurs entirely within the [INTERVIEWER]'s turn, where the interviewer recounts stories told by others (Kid Ori, Bud Scott, Mutt Carey) about Bolden's church background.

ctx.x: Well, how important was the religious feeling in influencing all of this? Well, I think that's difficult to say, too.

Of course, for people like me that came down here years after it started, I would never know. But other people like, say, Kid Ori, for instance, and some of the first people I met in California, like Bud Scott, one of the old-timers, quite a few of those said that a lot of the music came right out of the churches of the jazz bands as if... I know it was either Ori or Bud Scott. I don't remember which one. It could have been Mutt Carey. I'm talking about Buddy Bolden. They said, well, he got all of his music right…
What about the street marches, the funeral marches? Are they all the same thing?
